author: buchanan_robert
text:
The city waits to-morrow, and its face Is brown with dust and heat;

But now, when there is none

To think or suffer yet,
We will be glad as leaves that are bare In sunshine, and we shall not care

What is to come.

author: cushag
text:
The most that we can do is to die with honor;

And, if our chance be fair, to have won some fame
By deeds of love or hate — what better fate than this?

To fill our brief day's space with such work as may remain
Untarnished by regret or memory of shame.

Haiku: A three-line Japanese verse form consisting of 17 syllables arranged in five units, with the first line having 5 and second and third lines each containing 7 syllables, traditionally evoking images from nature (a word or phrase for example).

author: buchanan_robert
text: The two birds that were dead on the door step made me sad. I felt like taking them away from each other, but my mind refused to do so. The second day when i looked at those two birds I could feel their death. Their bodies turned cold and became lifeless. There were no signs of life left inside them. This is how i felt when I read this piece of writing.

author: buchanan_robert
text: When I first heard the news about my father’s death I could not believe it. As far as I knew he had been working on a project that would make us all rich when he completed it. He had already made millions and now we were going to be millionaires! Of course then I discovered this was just a rumor started by someone who wanted our inheritance for themselves but I still believed they were right because I loved my father so much. My dad was like no other person in my life; always kindhearted, generous and patient with me even though I am not an easy child.

There is so much that life can give,
This, it seems, are just the things we need,
I pray you take them kindly, please,
And give thanks for these beautiful things.

text:
Be sure you don't forget what you brought today,
Though I may leave it all behind,
I will keep this love within my heart always so true;
And there in time we shall meet again,
For when you go away, dear, be sure you do not forget!

author: john_keats
text:
Onward he moves through winding ways,
With light, nimble feet and darting gaze;
The sun’s last beams are gleaming bright,
As on their path they trace each sight.

His pace is sure, but not too fast,
Through chambers dim, where nothing past
But echoes come from far away,
To greet him as he passes by.

My mother calls me to her; she bids me come away with her.
She says: "Take your little brother by his hand and we will go."
"No," I say, "my dear, there are none else here, not even you!"

Tug-of-war with a donkey
In my memory I see me tugging
A stubborn, old and hairy donkey,
With one hand on his head and another on his tail.

My friend and I were so excited!
We wanted to have fun that day.
The donkeys we chose weren't very strong;
Our friends were tired before they had even started.

You get exactly the opposite!

text:
God bless all those brave seamen,
Who sail the oceans wild and free,
With joy unspeakable, as they ride,
The waves and wind with fearless pride.

But some must go before them,
To guide their ships through storms so grim,
They call upon their loved ones home,
In times of storm or danger dire.

Muzaffar Iqbal wrote this poem, which was translated into English by Michael Riffe:


I will give you the land
and I will make you its king;
you are not my son, nor am I your father-in-law;
I’ll just hand it over to you.

In return for my gift, you must feed me.

Do you want something from me?
Ask for whatever you like and take!

In the shadow of his dark-blue eyes,
We stand with bated breath and waiting,
For those blue shadows to come out,

And then we see them slowly rise,
As though they would not know their place;
The old ones never quite depart,
When you are trying to go at peace.

author: stephen_crane
text: In this piece I have attempted to write an original poetic composition which has been written with attention being paid to the rhyming and rhyme scheme that is characteristic of traditional poetry. The subject matter for my poem was taken from nature, specifically birds, and in particular from a scene in which they are engaged in some sort of activity; in my case it's the seemingly simple act of sitting in a line while one bird seems to be singing to himself (though there could be another meaning here as well).

author: thomas_hardy
text:
I heard a whispering voice call out,
“Where are you going?” I answered aloud,
To which my mind replied, “Home.”
It whispered further, “Why do you run?
What makes your heart beat so fast?
Is it because I am gone?”
The whisperer was right; the sound was mine!
Now that my mind is silent,
My heart still beats loudly;
Yet, how can I be sure if it is mine or his?

author: william_wordsworth

 Whence came it? when did it first start to bud ?

 And whence was brought the spirit that inspired

 The strength and majesty of this broad wood ?

 Why does this sapling now so tender grow,

 A little flower that will not long endure ?
